Sensor Monitoring

Understand what's in your indoor air

We deploy compact Aethair sensors in ~30 homes per neighborhood to continuously monitor fine particulate matter (PM2.5), temperature, and humidity — with no Wi-Fi needed.

Data collected across ~120 indoor and ~30 outdoor sensors will feed neighborhood-level predictive exposure models, giving us the most accurate picture of air quality conditions in Haddington, Point Breeze, Kingsessing, and Grays Ferry.

  • Tiny sensor: 4.3″ × 2.6″ × 1.2″ — just plug into a wall outlet
  • Monitors PM2.5, dry-bulb temperature, and humidity
  • No Wi-Fi required — transmits data automatically
  • Long-term campaign: Spring 2026 through Summer 2027

Air Cleaning Intervention

Reduce your indoor PM2.5 — for free

Participants receive a DIY Corsi-Rosenthal (CR) Box air cleaner, proven to significantly reduce fine particulate matter indoors. It's easy to build, easy to run — and you get to keep it.

Combined with personalized behavioral guidance on ventilation, masking, and home practices, our target is a 25% reduction in indoor PM2.5 exposure for participating households.

  • DIY air cleaner built from standard box fans + MERV-13 filters
  • 24″ × 24″ × 24″ — fits in any room
  • Workshops and guidance on ventilation and masking included
  • The CR Box is yours to keep after the study ends

Community Alert System

Real-time SMS alerts when it matters

Our data-driven SMS notification system informs residents when environmental conditions in their neighborhood warrant protective action — based on predictions from our exposure models.

Alerts are personalized, actionable, and easy to opt out of at any time. Delivered once or twice a week, they translate complex sensor data into simple, clear guidance.

  • "Run your CR Box now" — when indoor PM2.5 is elevated
  • "Open windows for fresh air" — when outdoor conditions are favorable
  • "Outdoor air pollution is high, stay inside" — on bad air days
  • Powered by neighborhood-scale predictive exposure models

Community Engagement

Driven by community, for the community

Every stage of this project is guided by trusted local partners. Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) and block captains lead outreach, recruitment, and ongoing engagement across all four neighborhoods.

We are training 25–50 high school Air Stewards to lead community education, assist with sensor installation, and interpret air quality data for their neighbors.

  • Haddington · Point Breeze · Kingsessing · Grays Ferry
  • Partnerships with local CBOs and block captains
  • Community workshops on ventilation and air quality
  • Youth Air Stewards trained as neighborhood educators

A 3-step approach to
cleaner indoor air

Simple, proven, and community-driven. Here's what participating in the study looks like.

01.

Host a Sensor

We install a small Aethair sensor in your living room to monitor your indoor air quality 24/7.

  • Just plug it into a wall outlet — no Wi-Fi needed
  • Tiny footprint (0.4 lbs, smaller than a paperback)
  • A Drexel team member handles installation
  • Sensor stays in place for the full 18-month campaign
Result: Your home contributes real data to neighborhood air quality maps and predictive models.
02.

Run a CR Box

Receive a free Corsi-Rosenthal Box air cleaner and guidance on how to use it to reduce PM2.5 in your home.

  • Easy-to-use DIY air cleaner — no assembly required
  • Workshop on ventilation and protective behaviors included
  • Pre- and post-intervention sensor data tracks your improvement
  • The CR Box is yours to keep after the study
Target: 25% reduction in indoor PM2.5 in participating homes.
03.

Receive Alerts

Opt into a weekly SMS alert system powered by our neighborhood exposure models — personalized, actionable, easy to cancel.

  • 1–2 text messages per week with air quality guidance
  • Alerts adapt to real-time conditions in your neighborhood
  • Tips like "Run your CR Box now" or "Great day to open windows"
  • Opt out at any time — no strings attached
Result: You make data-driven decisions every day to protect your household's health.

Eligibility

  • 18 years of age or older
  • Live in Haddington, Point Breeze, Kingsessing, or Grays Ferry
  • Willing to host a small indoor sensor
  • Able to run an indoor air purifier (24″ × 24″ × 24″)
  • Can complete activities in English
  • Able to provide informed consent
